# Results (generated by `scripts/stats.py` from `results/runs/*.json`)

## Falsifiable claim

At 95% sparsity (achieved 95.00%), fisher_taylor pruning reaches 97.97% +/- 0.15 test accuracy versus 98.15% +/- 0.11 for magnitude pruning (mean +/- std over 8 seeds; dense reference 97.69% +/- 0.23). Paired difference (fisher_taylor - magnitude) -0.18 pp, 95% bootstrap CI [-0.29, -0.07], exact sign-flip p = 0.0312, fisher_taylor better in 2/8 seeds. The 95% bootstrap CI excludes 0, so the gap is unlikely to be seed noise: magnitude is better by about 18 of 10,000 test images.

### Ablations at the same sparsity

- At 95%: fisher_taylor+regrow - fisher_taylor = +0.04 pp [-0.03, +0.10], fisher_taylor+regrow better in 5/8 seeds, p = 0.3047.
- At 95%: fisher_taylor - taylor1 = +0.29 pp [+0.19, +0.37], fisher_taylor better in 8/8 seeds, p = 0.0078.
- At 95%: fisher_taylor - fisher_taylor+oneshot = +0.56 pp [+0.46, +0.65], fisher_taylor better in 8/8 seeds, p = 0.0078.
